issues.failure_explanation: The appendix embedding is proved for the unrestricted parameter set \(\Omega=\R^d\times(0,\sigma_{\max}]\), where the center variable runs over all of \(\R^d\). The main RKBS \(\cV(D)\) is defined with the restricted parameter set \(\Omega=D_1\times(0,\sigma_{\max}]\), where centers are confined to a bounded neighborhood of \(D\). The Besov proof constructs measures with centers ranging over all of \(\R^d\), so it does not establish an embedding into the restricted-center space. Thus the stated inclusion of the PDE solution in \(\cV(D)\) is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: In this case, the PDE solution \(u\in \cU_o\) also lies in the RKBS \(\cV\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove a restricted-center embedding/representation theorem for \(\cV(D)\), or redefine the main RKBS with the unrestricted center domain used in the appendix and verify that the rest of the framework remains valid.
issues.overall_effect: The justification that the exact PDE solution belongs to the RKBS used throughout the paper fails for the main restricted parameter space. This weakens the second-case convergence discussion in Remark \ref{rmk:convergence}, which relies on boundedness of \(\|u^\delta\|_{\cV}\) when \(u\in\cV\).
issues.title: Restricted-center RKBS not covered by unrestricted Besov embedding
issues.why_classification: The main existence and representer results do not depend on this inclusion, but a stated convergence justification is lost; repairing it requires a new embedding or a global change of the parameter space, not a one-line correction.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma asserts a two-sided multiplicative quadrature equivalence uniformly over the whole \(\cV\)-norm ball. But \(\hat{L}\) depends only on finitely many point evaluations of the residual. Since \(\cV\) is infinite-dimensional, there are nonzero \(v\in\cV\) whose residual vanishes at all collocation points; after scaling, \(\|v\|_{\cV}\le M\), \(\hat{L}(v)=0\), while generally \(L(v)>0\). Hence \(L(v)\le 2\hat{L}(v)\) can fail for arbitrarily large \(K\). A bound on \(\|e\|_{C^{0,\gamma}}\) does not rule out this degeneracy.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exact two-sided lemma by a uniform quadrature estimate with an additive error term depending on \(M\) and \(K\) that tends to zero as \(K\) increases, and adjust the error-bound proof to include this term.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem \ref{thm:error_bound} relies on this false uniform equivalence to pass from empirical loss bounds to continuous-loss bounds. The finite-\(K\) error guarantee is therefore unsupported as written.
issues.title: Uniform quadrature equivalence over the entire RKBS ball is false
issues.why_classification: The lemma is false as stated, but a corrected additive-error quadrature estimate could plausibly preserve a comparable finite-\(K\) error bound; the repair is nontrivial but does not necessarily destroy the main result.

issues.failure_explanation: The support condition is derived from the stated characterization of \(\partial\|\bar\mu\|_{M(\Omega)}\) as continuous functions equal to \(\sgn\bar\mu\) on \(\supp\bar\mu\). For a general signed Radon measure with a non-atomic part and sign changes, \(\sgn\bar\mu\) is not defined pointwise and there may be no continuous function equal to it on the support. The proposition claims the condition for any solution, but it is valid only for finite atomic minimizers (whose existence is guaranteed by the representer theorem).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Proposition \ref{prop:added-1} to finite atomic minimizers, or use the correct subdifferential characterization in \(C_0(\Omega)^{**}\).
issues.overall_effect: The optimality/support condition is overclaimed for arbitrary solutions. The algorithmic use with finite atomic networks is unaffected once one restricts to the finite minimizer supplied by the representer theorem.
issues.title: Subdifferential characterization invalid for non-atomic measures
issues.why_classification: The paper already proves existence of a finite atomic solution, so a local restriction to that case repairs the statement without changing the practical dual-variable framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We use an empty network as the initialization of Algorithm \ref{alg:main} unless otherwise specified.

issues.failure_explanation: When the algorithm is initialized with an empty network, \(N^{(t)}=0\). The maximum over the empty index set \(1\le n\le 0\) is undefined, so Phase I is not well-defined at the first iteration. The subsequent insertion condition also uses \(p_0\).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define \(p_0=0\) when \(N^{(t)}=0\), or initialize with at least one kernel node.
issues.overall_effect: The stated algorithm cannot be executed exactly as written for the default empty-network initialization used in the experiments.
issues.title: Algorithm undefined for empty initial network
issues.why_classification: A standard degenerate-case convention fixes the issue without changing the algorithm's operation or guarantees.
